column7: The role->permission cache generation (system_metadata.role_permissions_generation) was bumped only by the application, so a direct database change to role_permissions or permissions (operator SQL, a script, a restore into a live database) kept authorizing from every running replica's cache until restart. Triggers on both tables (PostgreSQL statement-level ENABLE ALWAYS incl. TRUNCATE; SQLite per-row) now bump it in the writer's transaction, installed by the migration on fresh install and upgrade, and every generation read proves the triggers exist in the same statement: missing or disabled triggers bypass the cache (fail closed). Server-level: server/http TestFoldedCredential_CrossReplicaInvalidation role-permission-removed-direct-sql / permission-renamed-direct-sql (red on main, both backends). Postgres legs (truncate, replica-role session, disabled trigger) pg-gated in the same tests.
